Special Features of Iran’s Market
Daily price limits → buy and sell queues; in a crisis you may be unable to sell for several days (the limit percentage has changed several times; please check).
Trading halts before important announcements, general meetings or capital increases; sometimes long.
Quasi-state and holding-company major shareholders → conflicts of interest (related-party deals, dividends set by the major shareholder’s cash needs).
Low free float → the price can stay far from value for a long time.
A heavy government role: set prices, the official exchange rate, feedstock and energy prices, taxes and export duties.

Inflation and Real Return
Nominal Return Is Misleading
A 40% nominal return in a year with 45% inflation means you got poorer.
Example: 60% nominal and 40% inflation → 1.6 ÷ 1.4 − 1 = 14.3% (not 20%).
Three Benchmarks (Hurdles)
The nominal risk-free rate: the yield to maturity of Akhza or a fixed-income fund’s return. If a stock doesn’t beat it, you took risk for nothing.
Expected inflation: the minimum just to keep purchasing power.
People’s alternative assets: the dollar, gold coins and housing. Money moves between them.
Pricing Power
If a company can raise its selling price in step with inflation or the dollar, its nominal profit grows and the stock is inflation-proof.
If the selling price is set by the government or stays fixed while costs rise with inflation, inflation is the company’s enemy.
This is FIS’s most important first filter in Iran.
Difference from International Standards
Iranian financial statements are not adjusted for inflation (the equivalent of IAS 29 is not applied).
Old fixed assets are recorded at a low cost → depreciation below reality → accounting profit above economic profit.
Book value is below replacement value, so P/B means less in Iran.
Nominal return 60% and inflation 40%. What is the real return in percent?
1.6 ÷ 1.4 − 1 = 0.143, i.e. 14.3%. Simple subtraction (20%) is wrong.
Nominal return 40% and inflation 45%. Real return? (write a negative number with a minus sign)
1.4 ÷ 1.45 − 1 = −3.4%. You made a nominal profit but got poorer.
Nominal return 50% and inflation 30%. Real return?
Real return is calculated exactly with the formula “nominal return minus inflation”.
Subtraction is only an approximation and is far off when inflation is high. Use (1 + nominal) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1.

Gold, Silver, Coins or Stocks?
The Role of Each Asset

Dr. Khosravani sees dividend-focused stocks as the main engine of wealth, with part of your assets in gold and silver (bars or granules) to protect purchasing power. In his view gold beats the dollar in the long run.
In his view, for a non-expert, gold is safer than land.
He sees exchange-traded gold funds as a substitute for physical gold: no storage risk and no tax on buying physical gold (check the tax rules). But a fund can also carry a bubble.
And he sees a fixed-income fund returning less than inflation as an economic loss; only a short-term parking spot.

What Is a Bubble?
Bubble = the gap between the market price and intrinsic value.

Coins: intrinsic value = the coin’s pure gold weight × the price per gram of gold. In a Mordad 1404 (August 2025) video he said the Emami gold coin was not a good investment because of a bubble of about 10%.
In his view, silver funds can carry three bubbles stacked on top of each other: the dollar, the metal itself, and the gap between the fund’s price and its NAV.
A bubble means you pay more than the value; if it deflates, you lose even if the world price stays the same.

For years he has rated silver more attractive than gold for the long term, provided you account for its bubble.
In the same live stream he estimated the silver bubble in the physical market and on the commodity exchange at about 15 to 25% (Dey 1404, about January 2026; work out today’s number yourself).

Trading Code, Market Board and Smart Money
From Sign-up to Your First Purchase
1. Register and verify your identity in SEJAM (the comprehensive customer information system).
2. Choose a broker and get a trading code and online trading access.
3. Deposit money into your brokerage account and buy through the trading platform.
The identity checks and documents change from time to time (please check).
Three Numbers People Mix Up
Trading volume: the number of shares that changed hands today.
Trading value: the money that moved today = volume × price.
Market value: the price of the whole company = price × total number of shares.
High volume in a low-priced stock may be little money.
Trading value = volume × price\nMarket value = price × total number of shares
Retail, Institutional and Smart Money
“Retail” (haghighi) means individuals; “institutional” (hoghooghi) means entities (funds, companies, banks). tsetmc shows each group’s buying and selling separately.
A retail money inflow means retail buying exceeds retail selling. In the daily reports on his channel he tracks retail money flowing into and out of each industry.
“Smart money” in market slang: large retail purchases before the price moves; usually seen as a high average purchase per buyer and a retail buyer power above 1.
Writing filters: setting conditions on tsetmc market-watch data (for example buyer power above 2 and trading value above average) to find tickers that meet them.
Block trade: large blocks of shares changing hands between major holders; it shows at what price the big players are buying or selling.
Retail buyer power = average retail purchase per buyer ÷ average retail sale per seller

These are part of his course (smart money, filter writing, buying range), but stock selection is done with Codal and the Golden Three.
Market-board data is for timing: finding the buying range of a stock you have already judged to be good value.
Smart money also makes mistakes and can be faked; it is never the only reason to buy.
